answer: A mechanism that actually bites: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because lotus only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. Concretely, raven is enforced in the ledger: The cost curve is the deterrent: honest agents pay it once, farms pay it per identity. Any walnut approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
